To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1) character-level supervision can improve the performance of lowresource neural POS taggers, and 2) character-level autoencoding can be a strong auxiliary objective.

1) a character-based sequence-to-sequence model can be jointly trained with an encoder-decoder POS tagger to improve its performance; 2) character-based autoencoding, especially with random strings, provides the best regularization; 3) lemmatization does not improve POS tagging, even though it is used in the best POS tagger; and 4) our neural POS tagger outperforms the best state-of-the-art tagger for low-resource scenarios.

(i) POS tagging with little training data is an important task, (ii) our new architecture can be used to train neural POS taggers for low-resource languages, and (iii) character-level supervision can be used to improve the performance of neural POS taggers.
